scope: Two source-derived consumer assertions prompted by EC3330/366, integrated and passing; not whole-clause certification.

features.source: EC3 primary physical p.812 / printed p.797, Text annotation object 7872 at [30.058975,610.877869,54.058975,634.877869]. It says Lang entries are text strings, may be Unicode-encoded, and may be represented using literal or hexadecimal PDF string syntax.
features.implementation_and_assertions: PDF text strings are decoded generically before catalog and structure language handling. Existing public structure phrase-language tests exercise literal catalog/ancestor Lang, and hex Unicode Alt/E phrase strings; pdf-model language tests exercise literal Lang and other generic string tests cover Unicode hex decoding. No inspected assertion combines a hex-form Lang dictionary value with its effective language at a public consumer.
features.assessment: A small assertion specificity gap, not evidence of incorrect decoding: the draft checks catalog hex Lang fallback and a descendant hex Lang override through Viewer::AccessibilityTree while a literal ancestor Lang establishes precedence.

features.source: Table 8 on physical p.55 / printed p.40 has Text annotation object 1635 clarifying that predictor DecodeParms /BitsPerComponent has no relationship to the similarly named image dictionary key. Table 87 on physical p.274 / printed p.259 has paired StrikeOut/Caret annotations: Caret 3633 inserts 'the'; StrikeOut 3634 removes 'if a predictor function is used'. The resulting Table 87 text governs the image samples delivered by the filter. These source statements concern distinct producer/sample descriptions and do not, by themselves, mandate reader rejection of inconsistent files.
features.implementation_and_assertions: pdf-syntax applies a Flate stage's DecodeParms to predictor reconstruction; pdf-model image decoding separately reads image /BitsPerComponent to unpack the final decoded sample stream. Existing filter tests give independent decoded-byte oracles for predictor parameters; image-mask tests give raster sample oracles for image BPC, but no reviewed test passes differing predictor/image BPC through the same valid rendered image consumer.
features.assessment: A meaningful valid-input regression is feasible. The draft uses Flate to recover predictor-encoded ASCIIHex text, then ASCIIHexDecode to produce three bytes containing24 packed one-bit gray samples. DecodeParms uses BPC=8 over the intermediate text row; the image dictionary uses BPC=1 over the final 24 image samples. This makes the fields semantically and observably distinct, rather than testing a malformed producer mismatch or a geometry where both BPCs produce the same row length.

limits: Both tests PASS; model/core all-targets ClippyPASS. Parent added binary header comment, no-cut-chain guard, exactRGBA sample assertions, corrected return type and scoped lint expectations.

The image fixture's final decoded bytes are valid for Width=24, Height=1, DeviceGray, BPC=1. Its preceding predictor operates on an ASCIIHex representation, not on the final image samples; this is why BPC=8 and image BPC=1 can validly differ.
Neither issue establishes a whole-clause pass or a new malformed-file rejection obligation.
